svg.aria-label: How to write औ: 7 strokes · 6 pen lifts · 8 movements
svg.title: Writing औ
svg.desc: 8 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of औ (devanagari), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansDevanagari-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Saurmandal, ‘Devanagari औ stroke order.svg’, panels 1–7, Wikimedia Commons, 5 August 2023 <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Devanagari_%E0%A4%94_stroke_order.svg>. Source note on variation: The seven-panel diagram shows seven ordered pen-down runs. Panel 1 writes the joined upper-and-lower left body used for अ; panel 2 restarts at the middle and sweeps the shoulder right. Panels 3 and 4 separately descend the inner and trailing stems used for आ. Panels 5 and 6 each restart at the trailing stem's headline junction: first the lower upper arc sweeps upward and left, then the taller upper arc repeats that direction to its open tip. Panel 7 restarts at the headline's left edge and draws the shirorekhā left-to-right, for six intervening lifts. This learner path follows that modern printed teaching form and fits its turns and directions to Noto Sans Devanagari. Other traditions and everyday handwriting may divide or simplify the curves differently, so this is a sourced learner path rather than a universal standard.
svg.text: How it is written — 7 strokes · 6 pen lifts · 8 movements
Stroke order after Saurmandal, ‘Devanagari औ stroke order.svg’, panels 1–7, Wikimedia Commons, 5 August 2023
